correctness.rationale: For all n>=3, k>=2, h=min(k,n), the two independent hub fibers have h^2 choices. A degree-two list neighbor forbids at most one pair and a degree-two partial-matching DP fiber forbids at most two coordinate-disjoint pairs, proving sufficiency for n<h^2 and 2n<h^2 respectively. Disjoint ordinary hub lists realize all h^2 single exclusions; a cyclic one-factorization followed by pairing successive edges realizes all h^2 DP pair exclusions in ceil(h^2/2) degree-two neighbors. The crossing-boundary coordinates are distinct for odd h>=3, while no crossing occurs for even h. Cases k=1 and n=1,2 are separately addressed. Exact local-matching enumeration, direct obstruction replay and independent set-cover DP in verify.py corroborate the finite ingredients; infinite proof is written combinatorially.

Its general planar/minor-class theorems neither calculate the exact truncated list function for every n nor the exact two-choice DP obstruction capacity. A 2023 preprint covers K_{2,4}-minor-free graph classes, not K_{2,n} for n>=4. A 2026 study posted after the October 25 week anchor provides class-wide square-root bounds, not these exact K_{2,n} parameters. value.rationale: The same two-hub planar 2-connected obstruction family is used in recent degree-truncated coloring literature. The theorem resolves the exact truncated ordinary-list and correspondence-coloring thresholds for all n>=3; unlike the older single k^2 witness, it supplies sharp necessity and sufficiency across every n, exhibits a DP obstruction that packs two forbidden hub choices per degree-two neighbor, and proves a concrete unbounded additive gap and limiting ratio sqrt(2). These are natural extremal invariants with structural explanations rather than unmotivated isolated computations.
